item.title: AirAsia to delay staff salary payments to end of month, internal email shows – report
item.dc:creator: Yimie Yong
item.description: AirAsia has told employees it will delay salary payments to the end of each month from November through March.
item.content:encoded:
Malaysia-headquartered low budget carrier AirAsia has told employees it will delay salary payments to the end of each month from November through March, according to an internal email seen by Reuters.

The email, sent to Malaysia-based staff late last week by chief people officer Muhammad Khurram Zia, cited the need for a “temporary operational adjustment” at Southeast Asia’s largest budget airline, which like its peers faces higher jet fuel costs, Reuters reported on Friday.

Salary payments during the five-month period would be made on the 30th of each month or the last day of February, the email said. The company cited a “challenging environment” and asked employees for “patience and flexibility”, according to the report.

The email’s contents were confirmed by two people familiar with the matter. One of the people said AirAsia had previously paid salaries earlier in the second half of each month.

AirAsia did not respond to a request for comment, the report added.

AirAsia Philippines said on Thursday that it would reduce its workforce following sustained pressure on its operating costs, without specifying how many staff would be affected.

The airline said on Friday that it remained fully operational and committed to serving the Philippine market. The planned workforce adjustment will not affect passenger flights, booking or other services, AirAsia Philippines general manager and president Anna Victoria Lu said in a statement, Reuters reported.

The AirAsia Philippines Pilots’ Union filed notice of a strike after 90 pilots were retrenched, its president said in a video posted on social media on Thursday.

AirAsia reported its third consecutive quarterly loss on Monday. For the first nine months, net losses piled up to MYR857.16 million on revenue of MYR15.7 billion, earlier media reports showed.

In September this year, Capital A CEO and AirAsia Co-Founder Tony Fernandes refuted an earlier media report that said AirAsia needs government help to absorb the budget carrier’s domestic market share.

AirAsia’s Fernandes refutes report that AirAsia needs government bailout – report

item.title: Korea’s Jeju Semiconductor to take 65% of Vietnam memory packaging unit for $19.5M
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Jeju Semiconductor, a South Korean listed company, plans to take a 65 percent stake in a memory chip packaging and testing company in Vietnam for about KRW26 billion ($19.5 million).
item.content:encoded:
Jeju Semiconductor, a South Korean listed company, plans to take a 65 percent stake in a memory chip packaging and testing company in Vietnam for about KRW26 billion ($19.5 million).

In a filing with the Korean Exchange (KRX), Jeju Semiconductor said the new company is provisionally named H.O.A. Semiconductor. It will be based at Hoa Lac High-Tech Park in Hanoi, with registered capital of $30 million.

The company said it is setting up the unit to secure back-end capacity for memory chips, as it expects a sharp rise in wafer volumes from 2028. The filing gives the planned completion date as January 20, 2027.

Under a call option agreement, co-investor APACT Co., Ltd. may sell up to one-third of the new company’s shares to the Korean company within 24 months of the capital payment date.

The investment followed a meeting between Hanoi authorities and Jeju Semiconductor. In September 2026, during a visit to Seoul, Hanoi People’s Committee Chairman Vu Dai Thang met an investment alliance of Jeju Semiconductor, APACT, and Vietnam-based technology giant FPT.

The alliance proposed a packaging and testing plant of more than $100 million at Hoa Lac as they signed a memorandum of understanding. The target was to begin production in the first quarter of 2028. Hanoi said it wants the factory to form part of a wider chip ecosystem, linking manufacturing, research, chip design, and training with Hanoi’s universities.

Vietnam’s FPT, Japan’s SBI Holdings to collaborate in memory chip packaging plant

item.title: Vietnam’s VinEnergo breaks ground on 126 MWp solar energy project in Philippines
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: VinEnergo, the renewable energy arm of Vietnamese conglomerate Vingroup, has broken ground on a 126 MWp solar plant in Sagay City, Negros Occidental, the first project under its cooperation with the Philippine Department of Energy.
item.content:encoded:
VinEnergo, the renewable energy arm of Vietnamese conglomerate Vingroup, has broken ground on a 126 MWp solar plant in Sagay City, Negros Occidental, the first project under its cooperation with the Philippine Department of Energy.

In a statement on Friday, Vingroup said the move is a tangible step forward in VinEnergo’s commitment to investing in and advancing clean energy in the Philippines.

Previously, VinEnergo and the Philippine Department of Energy signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to establish a framework for cooperation in developing clean energy sources, laying the foundation for the research and implementation of large-scale energy projects across the country.

A key focus of the cooperation is the development of renewable energy projects integrated with energy storage systems, with a targeted renewable energy capacity of more than 20 GW and the potential to deliver up to 5 GW of baseload power to the Philippine national grid. The 126 MWp Sagay Solar project represents the first concrete step in advancing this cooperation, while paving the way for broader collaboration between VinEnergo and leading energy companies in the Philippines.

The 126 MWp Sagay Solar project is being developed in partnership with SunAsia Energy, a Philippine renewable energy company. The project features the innovative Solar on Stilts solution, which utilizes elevated solar panel structures to maximize space efficiency and optimize land use while generating clean electricity.

The project forms part of a broader 422 MWp portfolio jointly developed by VinEnergo and SunAsia Energy, comprising three projects in Macabebe, Sagay, and Silay. This portfolio underscores VinEnergo’s long-term commitment to working with local partners to unlock the Philippines’ renewable energy potential and contribute to the country’s energy transition.

Sharon S. Garin, Secretary of Energy of the Philippines, said “We welcome VinEnergo’s investment in the Philippine energy sector. The 126-megawatt-peak (MWp) Sagay Solar Power Project represents an important addition to the Philippines’ growing renewable energy capacity and our continuing efforts to strengthen national energy security. By harnessing our indigenous renewable energy resources, projects such as this help diversify our energy mix, reduce dependence on imported fuels, and lessen our exposure to volatility in international energy markets.”

Mr. Nguyen Anh Khoa, Chief Executive Officer of VinEnergo, said: “We believe that the energy transition is about more than simply expanding clean power generation; it is about building a sustainable energy system capable of supporting each country’s long-term development ambitions. For VinEnergo, the 126 MWp Sagay Solar project holds particular significance as the first concrete step in our strategic cooperation with the Philippine Department of Energy.”

item.title: Vietnam expects trade deal with US soon, tariff “much lower” than proposed 35%
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Vietnam and the United States sides are completing technical matters before signing a trade agreement and the tariff rate will be "much lower" than the maximum rate at 35 percent suggested by Washington for the 301 Investigations.
item.content:encoded:
Vietnam and the United States sides are completing technical matters before signing a trade agreement and the tariff rate will be “much lower” than the maximum rate at 35 percent suggested by Washington for the 301 Investigations.

Vietnam’s Prime Minister Le Minh Hung made the remarks published at a ceremony in Hanoi marking the 30th anniversary of Vietnam’s stock market. Vietnam had made “very strong” commitments in the negotiations, Hung said without further detail.

The US Trade Representative (USTR) said on Wednesday (November 25) that it had determined that structural excess capacity practices in 14 economies, including Vietnam, were unreasonable and burdened US commerce. For Vietnam, it proposed tariffs of up to 35 percent on all goods, net of existing Section 301 tariffs. It said it would consider adjusting the rate to 20 percent if Vietnam reaches a reciprocal trade agreement that responds to its findings.

The US cited Vietnam’s industrial and land planning, labor enforcement, financial repression, price regulation, failure to address imports, and investment from non-market economies. It said the practices were especially relevant to textiles, apparel and footwear, shipbuilding, cement, and information and communications technology.

The notice exempts four categories of goods from the proposed tariffs: articles already subject to Section 232 tariffs, including semiconductor articles, which are excluded rather than taxed on top; informational materials, donations and accompanied baggage; products listed by tariff subheading in an annex; and certain agglomerated iron ores.

The annex features some headings for semiconductor manufacturing equipment (8486) and semiconductor devices (8541 and 8542), computer (8471), computer parts and accessories (8473), mobile and network telephone equipment (8517.13 and 8517.62), solid-state storage (8523.51), and others.

The US will hold a public hearing in Washington on January 25, 2027, for further decision.

Vietnam urges swift US trade deal, final text already sent to Washington

item.title: Vietnam’s Viettel Telecom launches Starlink satellite Internet service
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Viettel Telecom, the telecommunications firm under Vietnamese technology giant Viettel, has begun offering Starlink satellite internet in Vietnam, giving users a connection option in remote, islands, and offshore areas with limited ground infrastructure.
item.content:encoded:
Viettel Telecom, the telecommunications firm under Vietnamese technology giant Viettel, has begun offering Starlink satellite internet in Vietnam, giving users a connection option in remote, islands, and offshore areas with limited ground infrastructure.

In a statement on Thursday, Viettel Telecom said packages start at VND1.59 million per month ($60), with genuine equipment from 9.3 million dong. Viettel Telecom and Starlink Services Vietnam signed a commercial cooperation contract in September 2026. Hanoi’s Department of Science and Technology then licensed a nationwide resale service on November 16.

Starlink uses low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites and the service can be connected quickly without laying cable or building a base station on site. Viettel said download speeds can exceed 400 Mb per second, with latency of 20 to 50 milliseconds under suitable conditions. It said the service suits video calls, online meetings, field data transfer, camera monitoring, and remote production management.

Viettel emphasized the service can support fishing and cargo vessels, offshore platforms, survey teams, outdoor events, and construction sites that lack telecommunications infrastructure. The equipment can run on backup batteries, solar power, or generators.

Viettel said the service complements its fiber, 4G, and 5G offerings, and provides a backup route if ground networks fail during storms, floods, or landslides. It said local authorities and rescue forces could utilize it to keep communications running and transmit images from disaster sites.

item.title: Hong Kong’s F&B firm Maxim’s, Tencent Cloud to expand AI, data partnership
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Maxim's Group, a Hong Kong-based food and beverage group, and Tencent Cloud, the cloud business of global technology company Tencent, will explore a strategic collaboration on cloud infrastructure, customer data, and artificial intelligence (AI).
item.content:encoded:
Maxim’s Group, a Hong Kong-based food and beverage group, and Tencent Cloud, the cloud business of global technology company Tencent, will explore a strategic collaboration on cloud infrastructure, customer data, and artificial intelligence (AI).

In a statement on Friday, Tencent Cloud said the cooperation can support “One Maxim’s” vision through cloud infrastructure, consumer ecosystem, and AI capabilities. The collaboration was announced at the 2026 Tencent Global Digital Ecosystem Summit.

The collaboration supports Maxim’s “From Bricks to Clicks” transformation agenda by strengthening connectivity across brands, markets and customer touchpoints while enabling a more connected and data-driven operating model across the Group.

Creating a More Connected Foundation Across Markets and Brands

Founded in 1956, Maxim’s Group operates more than 2,000 outlets across over 70 brands and employs more than 20,000 people. As part of its “One Maxim’s” strategy, the Group is focused on strengthening regional digital synergy, consolidating fragmented data and enabling more integrated operations across markets, brands and functions.

Tencent Cloud’s proven Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) capabilities provide a secure and scalable cloud foundation supporting this vision. With established connectivity across Hong Kong, Chinese Mainland and Southeast Asia, together with deployment options spanning public cloud, hybrid cloud and on-premises environments, Tencent Cloud enables Maxim’s to support cross-market operations while maintaining flexibility over data governance and residency requirements.

Poshu Yeung, Senior Vice President of Tencent Cloud and Head of Tencent Cloud International, said: “Maxim’s Group has built one of Asia’s most extensive food and beverage networks, connecting customers across brands, channels and markets. We are delighted to support Maxim’s Group by bringing together Tencent Cloud’s infrastructure, consumer ecosystem and AI technologies. Together, we aim to help create a more connected and data-driven operating model that strengthens collaboration across brands, enhances customer engagement and supports long-term growth ambitions.”

Louis Mah, Director, Group Information Technology of Maxim’s Group, said: “At Maxim’s, we are dedicated to connecting people with great food while driving positive innovation and collaboration to support our future growth. As we advance our ‘One Maxim’s’ vision and ‘From Bricks to Clicks’ transformation agenda, we are focused on creating stronger connections across our brands, customer experiences and operations. Through our collaboration with Tencent Cloud, we are strengthening the digital capabilities needed to create a more connected customer journey and build a more unified organization.”

Connecting Customers and Operations Through Data and AI

Maxim’s Group is advancing its omnichannelstrategy by strengthening direct engagement with customers across digital and physical touchpoints.

Building on the Group’s Eatizen loyalty program and its expansion into Chinese Mainland through its own Weixin/WeChat Mini Program, the collaboration leverages Tencent’s consumer ecosystem capabilities, including Mini Programs, live video, social CRM and marketing technologies, to deepen loyalty engagement, strengthen customer retention and support more personalized customer experiences.

As Maxim’s Group continues to strengthen the connection between customers, data and operations, AI is becoming an increasingly important part of the Group’s transformation agenda. Building on existing applications such as personalized offers, dynamic pricing and smart ordering, Tencent WorkBuddy, an enterprise AI workspace, helps employees streamline knowledge access, collaboration and routine tasks through AI-powered assistance, while the Agent Development Platform (ADP) provides a governed framework for building, deploying and managing AI agents across brands and markets.

By enabling a more centralized approach to AI across the organization, Maxim’s Group aims to improve operational efficiency, enhance employee productivity and deliver better customer experience. The initiative also supports the Group’s efforts to address industry-wide labor challenges through AI-enabled productivity improvements across frontline and back-office functions.

The collaboration reflects a shared vision ofsupporting Maxim’s Group’s “One Maxim’s” ambition through One Cloud, One Ecosystem and One AI Fabric. By bringing together cloud infrastructure, consumer ecosystem capabilities and enterprise AI technologies, Tencent Cloud and Maxim’s Group aim to connect brands, markets, operations and customer experiences more seamlessly while supporting the Group’s long-term growth and digital transformation objectives.

Tencent Cloud, WeesWares bring palm check-ins to Singapore senior care centres

item.title: Korea’s DongSin EF plans $1.8B green ammonia investment in Vietnam’s Lam Dong province
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Vietnam's Lam Dong province is considering a proposal by South Korea's DongSin EF to build a green ammonia project costing about $1.78 billion.
item.content:encoded:
Vietnam’s Lam Dong province is considering a proposal by South Korea’s DongSin EF to build a green ammonia project costing about $1.78 billion.

In a statement on Wednesday, Lam Dong People’s Committee said the South Korean firm made the proposal at a meeting with Deputy Chairman of the provincial People’s Committee Nguyen Ba Ut.

The company proposes an integrated plant combining a solar farm, water electrolysis, an ammonia synthesis complex, storage, and export facilities. The site would be in the Tuy Phong solar development area, about 18 kilometers from Vinh Tan port.

In phase one, the plant would produce 300,000 tons of green ammonia a year. It has a total investment of $1.782 billion, including construction, equipment, and financing costs during construction. The company said it hopes to raise capacity to 1.2 million tons a year over the long term. It plans to use solar power first and study wind power later.

Later phases would depend on the results of phase one, market commitments and the company’s financial capacity.

According to the company’s governance adviser, Na Dong Heon, the project is still at the research stage and is receiving funding from the South Korean government. The company wanted the provincial authorities to advise on the next steps, he added.

In reply, Ut said Lam Dong has strong potential for renewable energy, particularly wind and solar. Green hydrogen and ammonia projects fit national energy policy and the province’s development direction.

Officials said the proposal is consistent with Vietnam’s National Green Growth Strategy, its Hydrogen Energy Development Strategy and the adjusted Power Development Plan VIII.

item.title: Indonesia’s sovereign fund Danantara posts $14B net profit in 2025
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: Danantara Indonesia recorded a net profit of Rp203.4 trillion ($14 billion) for the nine-month period in its first consolidated financial statements for the 2025 financial year.
item.content:encoded:
Danantara Indonesia recorded a net profit of Rp203.4 trillion ($14 billion) for the nine-month period in its first consolidated financial statements for the 2025 financial year.

The net profit reflects nine months of portfolio performance following the in-kind transfer of State-Owned Enterprise (SOE) shares in March 2025, and is supported by operating revenue of Rp2,385.2 trillion and net cash flow from operating activities of Rp563.1 trillion, the firm said in a statement on Wednesday.

This performance strengthens Danantara Indonesia’s capacity to drive national economic growth through SOE transformation and investment in productive sectors.

As of December 31, 2025, its total consolidated assets stood at Rp11,607 trillion. Meanwhile, on a 12-month pro forma basis, return on equity (ROE) reached 8.7 percent.

Danantara Indonesia Chief Executive Officer Rosan Roeslani said the results demonstrate the strength and productivity of the portfolio managed by Danantara Indonesia.

“For the first time, the performance of Danantara Indonesia’s entire portfolio is presented in a single set of audited consolidated financial statements,

“The results show a portfolio of significant scale, capable of generating healthy profitability and cash flow, and contributing to national economic activity. This foundation is our starting point to continue improving asset productivity and creating long-term value for Indonesia,” he added.

For the audited consolidation period from April to December 2025, Danantara Indonesia recorded operating revenue of Rp2,385.2 trillion and net profit of Rp203.4 trillion. Net cash flow from operating activities reached Rp563.1 trillion, while the debt-to-equity ratio was maintained at 0.54 times.

Financing and investment activity also increased, with loans and financing receivables growing 7.2 percent to Rp3,998.9 trillion and investments in securities rising 11.1 percent to Rp1,485.9 trillion.

The Danantara Indonesia ecosystem also paid Rp567.2 trillion in taxes in 2025, while State Capital Participation (PMN) allocations declined from Rp54.6 trillion in 2022 to Rp4.7 trillion in 2025.

“Danantara Indonesia’s success is measured not only by the size of its assets, but by its ability to make them more productive, generate sustainable returns and deliver real impact for the economy. Investment discipline, SOE transformation and governance will remain our priorities in the years ahead,” Rosan said.

Danantara Indonesia said it is following a phased roadmap to build the institution, strengthen its capabilities and sustain long-term value creation.

Having laid its institutional foundations in 2025, the fund is entering a phase of expanded transformation in 2026–2027.

The focus is on business transformation and restructuring across its portfolio companies, portfolio diversification, consistent returns, and a stronger capital structure and talent ecosystem.

In 2028–2029, Danantara Indonesia said it will focus on building Indonesia Global Champions in strategic sectors and strengthening its position as a world-class sovereign fund.

In support of national down streaming, the fund has begun developing more than 20 down streaming projects worth approximately Rp225 trillion across energy, minerals and metals, and food and agro-industry.

SOE transformation through Danantara Asset Management (DAM) also continued to accelerate. As of October 2026, 364 of approximately 1,074 SOE entities had been streamlined toward a target of 250–300 entities, with potential efficiencies of up to Rp50 trillion a year.

Performance improvements are beginning to show, including Garuda Indonesia adding 20 serviceable aircraft to reach 104 as of September 2026, and Krakatau Steel turning a $105.38 million loss in the first half of 2025 into a $10.94 million profit in the first half of 2026.

DAM has also driven the consolidation of Pertamina’s downstream businesses, as well as the establishment of Danareksa Investments, formed through the merger of four SOE investment management companies with more than Rp170 trillion in assets under management.

On the investment side, Danantara Investment Management (DIM) is targeting $3.8 billion in private investments to be deployed and signed in 2026.

As of October 2026, total investment assets stood at approximately Rp162 trillion, including Rp60.6 trillion in public investments.

Several strategic investments have moved into execution. The national Waste-to-Energy (PSEL) program across 33 regencies/cities is valued at approximately Rp40–50 trillion, with DIM’s investment of around Rp10 trillion serving as a catalyst.

DIM has also strengthened the Hajj and Umrah ecosystem through the acquisition of the 1,461-room Novotel Thakher Makkah and 4.4 hectares of land; invested in the Chlor Alkali–Ethylene Dichloride (CA-EDC) project, which is approximately 80 percent constructed; and signed an investment for a 25 percent stake in JBS’s protein business in Australia and New Zealand.

Danantara CIO Pandu Sjahrir says Indonesian corporate fundamentals remain strong despite market concerns

item.title: Catcha Digital’s net profit jumps more than two folds to $1.67M in Q3 on higher revenue
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: Malaysia's technology firm Catcha Digital Berhad has reported two times jump in its net profit to MYR 6.88 million ($1.67 million) in the third quarter ended 31 December, 2026 amid an increase in revenue.
item.content:encoded:
Malaysia’s technology firm Catcha Digital Berhad has reported two times jump in its net profit to MYR 6.88 million ($1.67 million) in the third quarter ended 31 December, 2026 amid an increase in revenue.

The firm’s revenue for the quarter surged 69.44 percent year on year to MYR 42.8 million ringgit, mainly driven by higher experiential advertising and digital advertising revenue, it said in a statement on Wednesday.

As for the first nine months ended September 30, 2026, the firm’s net profit slipped 11.25 percent year on year to MYR 5.18 million while its revenue soared 90.41 percent year on year to MYR 90.49 million.

“We are deeply inspired by Berkshire Hathaway to be the permanent home for market-leading companies in Southeast Asia. We acquire these companies, work with their founders to grow them organically, and reinvest the cash flow generated into the next acquisition,

“This quarter showed that the flywheel has started spinning and delivered our biggest quarter ever both in revenue and profits,” said Eric Tan, Group Chief Executive Officer of Catcha Digital.

All three flagship expos, Agri Malaysia, MBAM OneBuild and the Malaysian International Food and Beverage Exhibition (MIFB), were held in the third quarter, the segment’s peak quarter.

The firm’s cash and cash equivalents were MYR 31.70 million at September 30, 2026, against bank borrowings of MYR 12.29 million under a MYR 35 million revolving credit facility with Affin Hwang Investment Bank Berhad. Up to MYR 73.9 million more is available from outstanding warrants as a reserve source.

The firm highlighted that its growth is funded first from free cash flow and vendor financing, then debt, then equity.

“Nine months into 2026, the Catcha Digital platform is compounding as we intended. With eight acquisitions now contributing across three verticals, we expect a meaningfully stronger FY2026 than FY2025,

“We will continue to pursue strategic partnerships, investments and acquisitions that are directly accretive to our earnings per share,” said Patrick Grove, Chairman of Catcha Digital.

Catcha Digital said it has completed eight acquisitions since 2025, each positioned to strengthen its foothold in the digital media, business to business (B2B) expo and information technology (IT) solutions space, all expected to contribute positively to future earnings. No new acquisitions were completed during the third quarter of FY2026.

Malaysia’s Catcha Digital slips into the red despite higher revenue

item.title: ZTE partners True Corp to unveil TDD dual-band AAU solution in Thailand
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: ZTE Corporation, a Chinese provider of integrated information and communication technology solutions, has partnered with True Corporation, Thailand's telecom-tech company, to deploy a TDD dual-band AAU solution for 5G-Advanced and future evolution.
item.content:encoded:
ZTE Corporation, a Chinese provider of integrated information and communication technology solutions, has partnered with True Corporation, Thailand’s telecom-tech company, to deploy a TDD dual-band AAU solution for 5G-Advanced and future evolution.

Designed for high integration, wide coverage, large capacity, and lower power consumption, the solution is intended to enhance network quality and efficiency and provide wireless support for individual users, industry digitalization, and computing power networks, the duo said in a statement.

As Thailand’s digital economy accelerates, with explosive traffic growth, wider adoption of AI-capable devices, and deeper industry applications, wireless networks now face rising demands for bandwidth, latency, coverage, and energy performance.

TRUE continues to advance its premium network construction, while ZTE remains focused on innovation in wireless access and Massive MIMO.

In this collaboration, TRUE specified the performance targets based on its network requirements, and ZTE customized the A9651D M2326 accordingly.

Following joint single-site and first-cluster POC test validation, the equipment has been deployed at scale in TRUE’s network. This deployment reflects the technical collaboration between TRUE and ZTE to improve network performance and energy efficiency.

According to the results of joint field tests conducted in TRUE’s network, large-scale antenna arrays and intelligent beamforming enable the A9651D M2326 to achieve a 116 percent improvement in 2.6 GHz traffic compared with data measured before the first-cluster POC site test, attain 1.7Gbps throughput via SA NR CA (700+2300+2600), and successfully enable LTE 7CC CA.

By consolidating two TDD bands into a single AAU, the solution can reduce TDD RF units by 57 percent and overall weight by 30 percent compared with deploying separate single-band units, enabling rapid deployment across urban, suburban, and all other scenarios.

On energy efficiency, ZTE’s innovative Super-N2.0 solution enhances PA efficiency.

According to the field test results, after upgrading to the new equipment, site energy consumption was reduced by 11 percent compared with deploying separate single-band units.

It enables low-carbon operation while ensuring performance, helping operators pursue global decarbonization objectives such as net-zero targets and science‑based emissions reductions, and reducing long-term operating costs.

The solution supports one-step TDD deployment and is positioned for future spectrum evolution and 5G-Advanced new features and solutions, delivering long-term benefits from a single deployment.

This collaboration supports TRUE’s network requirements through equipment customization, joint testing, and commercial deployment, said the statement.

Malaysia’s U Mobile, ZTE test three-day off-grid 5G deployment in East Malaysia
